en.name: Edamame, frozen
en.summary: Frozen edamame keeps 2 years from purchase at −18 °C (0 °F) for best quality, and 1 week in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below once it has thawed. The freezer figure is a quality window, not a safety limit: edamame kept continuously at −18 °C stays safe indefinitely.
en.pantry: No room-temperature storage. Edamame is blanched before freezing and is a moist, low-acid vegetable once it warms up, so a bag left on the counter goes through the danger zone of 4–60 °C (40–140 °F) and follows the two-hour rule — one hour if the kitchen is above 32 °C (90 °F). There is no reason to do it anyway: frozen pods go straight into boiling salted water, or into a steamer, and are ready in minutes.
en.fridge: 1 week at 4 °C (40 °F) or below after thawing, kept covered. This is the figure for edamame that has been thawed but not yet cooked; cooked pods you have salted and chilled for the fridge are best eaten within a few days. Thawing in the fridge is also the only thawing method worth using, and it has a practical advantage: pods thawed cold and still at or below 4 °C may be refrozen with some quality loss, which is not true of pods thawed on the counter.
en.freezer: 2 years from purchase at −18 °C (0 °F) for best quality — an unusually long window, because the pods were blanched, which knocks out the enzymes that would otherwise slowly degrade colour and flavour. Kept continuously frozen they stay safe well beyond that; what you are watching for is freezer burn, dry white patches and pods welded into a solid block. Reseal the bag tightly with the air pressed out each time, and keep it away from the freezer door.
en.thawing: There is usually no need to thaw: boil or steam the pods straight from frozen. To thaw for a salad, do it in the fridge, never on the counter or in warm water. Pods thawed in the fridge and still cold may be refrozen; pods thawed warm may not.
spoilage: Dry, whitish, shrivelled pods — freezer burn, a quality fault rather than a safety one.
A solid block of pods frozen together, meaning the bag part-thawed and refroze.
Yellowed or brown pods, which means the colour has gone and the flavour with it.
A sour or fermented smell from thawed or cooked edamame kept too long.
tips: Cook straight from frozen; the pods need only a few minutes in boiling salted water.
Press the air out of the bag each time — air is what causes freezer burn.
Salt the water generously and salt the pods again while hot.
Keep the bag at the back of the freezer, not in the door.

faq.q: How long does frozen edamame last?
faq.a: 2 years from purchase at −18 °C (0 °F) for best quality. It stays safe longer if it never thaws; the window is about freezer burn and flavour.

faq.q: How long does thawed edamame keep in the fridge?
faq.a: 1 week at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, kept covered.

faq.q: Do you have to thaw frozen edamame?
faq.a: No. Boil or steam it straight from frozen — it takes only a few minutes and the texture is better than after thawing.

zh.name: 冷凍毛豆
zh.summary: 冷凍毛豆在 −18 °C 下自購買日起可保有最佳品質 2 年；解凍後放 4 °C 以下冷藏則是 1 週。冷凍那個數字是品質期限，不是安全上限：全程維持在 −18 °C 的毛豆可以無限期保持安全。
zh.pantry: 沒有室溫保存這一項。毛豆冷凍前汆燙過，回溫之後就是一種含水量高、低酸的蔬菜，所以一包放在檯面上的毛豆正在穿過 4～60 °C 的危險溫度帶，適用兩小時原則；廚房超過 32 °C 時只有一小時。而且本來就沒必要這樣做：冷凍毛豆莢直接丟進滾的鹽水或蒸籠，幾分鐘就好了。
zh.fridge: 解凍後蓋好放 4 °C 以下 1 週。這是「已解凍但還沒煮」的毛豆的期限；已經煮好、拌鹽冰起來的，最好幾天內吃完。冷藏也是唯一值得用的解凍方式，而且有個實際好處：在低溫解凍、始終維持在 4 °C 以下的毛豆可以再冷凍，只是品質會打折——在檯面上解凍的就不行。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下自購買日起 2 年品質最好——這是異常長的期限，因為毛豆冷凍前汆燙過，把那些會慢慢讓顏色和風味衰退的酵素先滅掉了。只要全程沒退冰，超過這段時間仍然安全；你要盯的是凍燒、乾白斑塊，以及整包凍成一大塊。每次用完都把空氣壓掉、確實封好，並且放在遠離冷凍櫃門的地方。
zh.thawing: 通常不必解凍：直接從冷凍下滾水煮或上蒸籠。要做成沙拉才需要解凍的話，請放冷藏，絕對不要放檯面或泡溫水。在冷藏解凍、還是冰的可以再冷凍；回溫過的不行。
spoilage: 豆莢變得乾白、皺縮——那是凍燒，屬於品質問題而不是安全問題。
整包凍成一大塊，表示它曾經半退冰又再凍回去。
豆莢發黃或變褐，表示顏色沒了，風味也跟著沒了。
解凍或煮過的毛豆放太久，聞起來發酸或有發酵味。
tips: 直接從冷凍煮；滾鹽水裡幾分鐘就夠。
每次都把袋子裡的空氣壓掉——凍燒就是空氣造成的。
煮的水要夠鹹，起鍋趁熱再補一次鹽。
袋子放冷凍櫃深處，不要放門邊。

faq.a: −18 °C 下自購買日起 2 年品質最好。只要沒退冰，放更久仍然安全；這個期限講的是凍燒和風味。

faq.q: 解凍後的毛豆冷藏可以放多久？
faq.a: 蓋好放 4 °C 以下 1 週。
不用。直接從冷凍煮或蒸，幾分鐘就好，口感也比退冰後更好。
